category: Devices for Measuring the Continuous Passage of Time
explanation: Sundials, hourglasses, water clocks, and atomic clocks are all instruments designed to actively measure the continuous flow of time. A calendar is a system for organizing and marking periods of time, but it does not actively measure its passage.

The Arch, Aqueduct, Colosseum, and Concrete are all iconic elements or materials fundamental to Ancient Roman engineering and architecture. A Pyramid is a monumental structure primarily associated with Ancient Egyptian and Mesoamerican civilizations, not Roman.
Meter, Liter, Gram, and Celsius are all fundamental units within the metric system. Inch is a unit of length from the imperial system.
